I’ll audit the current diff against the requested OAuth production scope, including repository instructions, manifests, and affected tests. I’ll keep this read-only and report only introduced, evidence-backed issues.

The new device flow is present through client, Nitro routes, and token refresh. I’m checking whether it actually reaches a selectable Copilot model and whether the production/validation contract is covered, rather than treating route registration as end-to-end proof.

Findings:

- High — incomplete integration — [oauth.ts:486](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/oauth.ts:486) enables Copilot OAuth and [CloudProviderKeysSection.tsx:198](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/components/settings/CloudProviderKeysSection.tsx:198) reports it as signed in, but no selectable Copilot model is integrated. The existing selector only appends `getModels(provider)` ([provider-models.ts:467](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/lib/provider-models.ts:467)); the installed Pi compatibility catalog returns zero models for `github-copilot`, and neither fallback list ([line 384](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/lib/provider-models.ts:384)) nor unavailable-model recovery ([line 411](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/lib/provider-models.ts:411)) includes it. Result: the production device login can succeed but supplies no usable model to select/run. Confidence: high.

- Medium — test coverage — [oauth.test.ts:110](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/test/oauth.test.ts:110) covers mocked upstream helpers and refresh, but does not exercise the browser orchestration added in [oauth.ts:137](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/oauth.ts:137) and [oauth.ts:339](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/oauth.ts:339): device response persistence, polling/status handling, credential save, and UI state transition. Thus the new end-to-end path can regress while the focused suite remains green. `bun test src/test/oauth.test.ts` passes 15/15. Confidence: high.

- Medium — documentation/implementation mismatch — [docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:13](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:13) states that `devenv shell` runs `keating:install` on first entry, but [devenv.nix:35](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/devenv.nix:35) merely defines an explicitly invoked task; there is no `enterShell`, task dependency, or other automatic invocation. New contributors can enter the shell without dependencies installed despite the documentation’s guarantee. Confidence: high.

- Medium — instruction-file disobeyed — the task-runner migration conflicts with [AGENTS.md:26](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/AGENTS.md:26)-[46](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/AGENTS.md:46), which requires `just` as the canonical workflow. The new [README.md:198](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/README.md:198) and [devenv.nix:4](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/devenv.nix:4) instead remove it in favor of namespaced devenv tasks. Confidence: high.

No concrete introduced finding in commit-message mismatch (OAuth edits are uncommitted), abstraction violation, dependency management, or insecure-code checks. `git diff --check` is clean; package manifests/locks are unchanged.
